a843b38d9b28e08b: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 11 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is examining claims that Anthropic’s Claude artificial intelligence platform was used to operate a commercial election manipulation campaign targeting users in Malaysia.
MCMC said it took the US AI company’s latest report seriously but stressed that the activities described fell outside its functions and mandate.
“MCMC was not involved in any activities or dealings as described in the report,” it said in a statement today.
Anthropic reportedly said it had identified and removed an account linked to a network of about 1,000 fake accounts on X, a fake news website and several fabricated dossiers or intelligence files.
MCMC said it was seeking further information and clarification from the relevant parties to establish the facts and understand the context of the claims.
“Based on the information and evidence obtained, MCMC will determine the appropriate follow-up action within its jurisdiction, including working with the relevant authorities,” it said.
The commission added that protecting the public from online harm and maintaining a safe and trusted online environment remained central to its responsibilities. — Bernama
edc42a9ab7db8527: TORONTO, Sept 12 — British actor Gary Oldman today backed his Slow Horses co-star Jack Lowden to be the new James Bond, as rumors swirl that the next 007 has been cast.
The veteran performer had caused a stir over the weekend when he appeared to suggest that Lowden had it in the bag.

But yesterday, he told reporters at the Toronto International Film Festival that he didn’t have the inside track on one of the most eagerly awaited casting decisions of the decade, but was definitely rooting for his colleague.

“I simply said: ‘Well, I believe that they’ve chosen the guy... and Jack is on the list,’ and I said: ‘Fingers crossed for Jack’, and then that was reported that I had some inside information,” Oldman said.
“I don’t know any more than you do. There’s six candidates. The rumor is that they’ve made their pick, but we don’t know who it is, and they’re waiting to announce it.”
Still, said Oldman, the 36-year-old Lowden would be a great choice to fill a role previously occupied by Daniel Craig, Roger Moore and Sean Connery, amongst others.
“Jack is... young, he’s masculine, he’s incredibly funny, which I think is important,” the Oscar winner said.
Lowden is also Scottish, which might work in his favor, said Oldman, adding it was “a nod to Sean Connery” that might chime with producers carrying the weight of a franchise rich in history.
“Part of the recipe for Bond, he’s got to have his sort of tongue in his cheek slightly, and a twinkle in his eye, and Jack Lowden has those qualities.
“And he’s a lovely guy to boot,” said the Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Spy star.
The most recent outing for 007 was No Time to Die—Craig’s last turn as the super spy—way back in 2021.

Since then, Amazon MGM has acquired creative control of the franchise, announcing the new installment will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, with a screenplay by Steven Knight, the creator of Peaky Blinders.

Knight recently hinted that a decision on an actor was imminent, with stars including Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Tom Holland, Harris Dickinson, Jacob Elordi and Kingsley Ben-Adir all previously linked with the role.
A joy
Oldman has worked with Lowden since the start of Slow Horses, the sixth season of which hits Apple TV next week.

New challenges await the dishevelled Agent Jack Lamb (Oldham) and his young protege, River Cartwright (Lowden), in the series about outcasts from Britain’s domestic spy services, based on the books by British author Mick Herron.
Oldman said it was a pleasure to be part of a cast that has real connections.
“We’ve been together since day one... and we all get on,” he said, describing how much he misses his colleagues in between seasons.
“As we get closer to coming back to do the show, often I’m quite excited to just get on the plane and get to see the gang.”
Playing Lamb—known for his threadbare socks, love of greasy food, and unkempt hair—“has been a joy,” but noted that the question his colleagues hear most often is whether he smells bad.
“And I don’t!” he laughed.
The show began filming during the Covid pandemic era, and already has a seventh season lined up.
Oldman said there appeared to be no end in sight.
“There’s no regrets to doing a show this long, and as long as Apple keep us on the air, we’ll see what happens in the future.
“But I’ve loved—absolutely adored—doing it.” — AFP
923e084fc9a75162: Man arrested over alleged murder of mother in Tambunan
KOTA KINABALU: Police arrested a 31-year-old man on suspicion of murdering his mother at a rented house in Kampung Katagayan, Tambunan, yesterday.
Keningau district police chief superintendent Erwansyah Abdul Basir said police were alerted to the incident involving the 56-year-old victim at about 2pm and subsequently tracked down the suspect.
He said preliminary investigations found that the victim died at the scene from injuries believed to have been inflicted with a sharp weapon.
"Villagers apprehended the suspect at a hut in Kampung Sutung, Tambunan, before handing him over to police.

"The suspect was taken to the Tambunan police station, where he was arrested by the Criminal Investigation Department team from the Keningau district police headquarters," he said in a statement today.
Erwansyah said the investigation team and forensic personnel had inspected the scene and seized several items believed to be linked to the case.
He said the victim's body had been sent to the hospital for a post-mortem examination and the case was being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
"The public is urged not to speculate or spread unverified information about the case," he said.

20f6735df0a49de4: NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is scheduled to have three bilateral meetings today on the sidelines of the 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit here.
The day starts off with a bilateral meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, followed by one with Anwar’s Indian counterpart and summit host Narendra Modi.
His third bilateral meeting is with Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed.
The Prime Minister is also scheduled to have a pull aside meeting with Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev.

This will be followed by one-on-one business meetings, including with Adani Group, which has positioned itself to be the market leader in its transport logistics and energy utility portfolio businesses focusing on large scale infrastructure development in India.

Also lined up are Segula Technologies India Pvt Ltd, a global engineering group; AWL Agri Business Ltd, one of India’s largest food and fast-moving consumer goods companies; and Motherson Group, a leading global design, engineering, manufacturing, assembly, and logistics specialist.

Later in the day, the Prime Minister will attend a gala dinner for leaders of BRICS member, partner and outreach countries at the Bharat Mandapan, the exhibition and convention centre where the summit will take place.
The summit, themed “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”, will focus on strengthening resilience, economic cooperation as well as trade and investment reforms.
As a founding member of BRICS, India has previously held its chairship three times — in 2012, 2016 and 2021. India assumed its fourth BRICS chairship on January 1, 2026.
Malaysia’s participation in the BRICS Leaders’ Summit is in its capacity as a BRICS partner country since January 1, 2025. — Bernama
094c69a2e52cb28d: PARIS, Sept 12 — A train carrying 186 passengers derailed in north-west France on Friday, injuring 44 people, one of them seriously, officials said.
The train was running between the Normandy cities of Rouen and Caen, Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot said on X.
It derailed around 7.45 pm (1745 GMT), local authorities said in a statement, and a mass-casualty response plan had been activated, with 130 firefighters, five medical teams and 80 vehicles deployed.
“Suddenly there were a few jolts, and then after about three seconds it got stronger and stronger,” one of the passengers, Louis, 24, told ICI Normandie radio.
“I couldn’t stay in my seat any more,” he said. “The windows partially shattered, the stones from the track came into the carriage. It was really shocking. I’m still shaking.”

Rouen prosecutor Sebastien Gallois said 44 people were injured including an 18-year-old woman evacuated “in a critical condition”, while tests for drugs and alcohol on the train driver had come back negative.
SNCF Reseau, which controls the French rail network, told AFP that traffic on the line has been suspended and power to the tracks cut to allow emergency services to operate.
“The priority is to care for the passengers and then to restore safe operating conditions,” SNCF Reseau said.
Rail authorities and the police are investigating the causes of the accident. — AFP
9f88c4abe1e25dca: SEPT 12 — It’s always nice to see a filmmaker return to their trashy, low-budget roots after a stint with the major studios.
For the better part of a decade, Adam Wingard has been somewhat lost inside the corporate machinery of Hollywood’s franchise industrial complex.

While his Godzilla vs. Kong entries were undeniably slick, big budget spectacles (and a whole lot of fun in their own special ways), they inevitably lacked the mean-spirited ingenuity, efficiency, and blood-soaked thrill of his early work.
Which is why Onslaught, which opened in Malaysian cinemas just last week, feels like such a breath of fresh air, especially when released just as the summer movie season ends.
Stripping away the CGI giant monsters, Wingard goes down and dirty again with a modestly budgeted, lean and mean genre entry.

It is clearly Wingard going back to making the exact type of films that made his name in the first place — sturdy, efficient, and wonderfully gory siege cinema — cut from the exact same cloth as You’re Next and The Guest.
In fact, comparing Onslaught directly to The Guest reveals just how much Wingard thrives when he operates within self-imposed boundaries.

The Guest succeeded because it took a simple, archetypal narrative, that of the mysterious stranger invading a family home, and injected it with relentless John Carpenter-esque dread, retro 1980s neon-soaked aesthetics, and a deliciously unhinged performance from Dan Stevens.

Onslaught functions on a very similar frequency. Swap out the quiet suburban house for an isolated, run down trailer park, and swap out Dan Stevens' super soldier for a trio of escaped, genetically modified super soldiers, and you have a film that plays almost like a disguised remake, reboot or even a sequel to The Guest.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Official posters for Adam Wingard’s action thriller ‘Onslaught’, starring Adria Arjona as former army sniper Celeste. — Picture via A24

Like all good siege films, Onslaught is an unabashed love letter to Carpenter, specifically his eternal classics Assault on Precinct 13 and Escape From New York, with a healthy dose of James Cameron’s The Terminator thrown into the mix for good measure.
Wingard captures that precise 70s/80s genre cadence — an isolated setting, a ticking clock, and an unstoppable force pounding at the gates — with perfect ease.
Where The Guest had Dan Stevens effortlessly charming and terrifying us in equal measure, Onslaught hands the emotional heavy lifting to Adria Arjona.
Fresh off impressive turns in Andor and Blink Twice, Arjona is a total badass lead here, and will remind Wingard fans of the similarly badass lead performance by Sharni Vinson in You’re Next.
She plays Celeste, a former Army sniper trying to keep her life together, with a raw, grounded physicality that makes every tactical manoeuvre and brutal exchange feel earned.
Having said that, Stevens isn't left out of the fun. Reuniting with Wingard 12 years after The Guest, Stevens flips his role from mysterious anti-hero to outright villain.
He has an absolute blast chewing the scenery as the wild, mad scientist figure behind the super soldier project, and I loved every second of his performance.
It’s the kind of uninhibited, gleeful work that reminds you why genre cinema can be so much fun when actors completely commit to the bit.
Yet, amid all the flying limbs and bullet riddled walls, the film's most delightful surprise is young Blake Kennedy as Celeste's daughter, Daisy.
Instead of playing the typical screaming child who exists purely to be rescued in most movies, Daisy is written and played as a proper, polite little lady.
Her pristine manners in the middle of absolute carnage inject a subtle, quirky and pitch-perfect element of comedy into the proceedings, giving the tension room to breathe.
If I had to complain about at least one thing, it would have to be the final stretch.

Onslaught builds up such a fantastic momentum during its first two acts that the final battle between Celeste and the last surviving super soldier didn't feel quite as epic or brutally difficult as what some fans might expect from a true final boss fight.
Some might even call it anti-climactic, that’s how underwhelming that final boss fight was.

Were parts of it censored because of extreme violence? It could be, but I can only find out once the film is out on digital, so as of now, it’s a wee bit underwhelming for my gore loving tastes. But that’s just me nitpicking.

Overall, Onslaught is a very solid piece of genre entertainment, especially during that remarkably exciting buildup, that proves Wingard is still at his absolute best when he forgets the studio green screens and goes back to basics.

8d6840158a21ff46: SEOUL, Sept 12 — North Korea fired an unidentified projectile toward the Sea of Japan on Saturday, South Korea’s defence ministry said.
The South’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said it detected the launch toward the body of water that Koreans call the East Sea but it gave no details.
The report came a day after South Korea concluded five days of joint maritime drills with the United States and Japan that were focused on North Korea.
Late last month North Korea slammed plans for the so-called Freedom Edge exercises in international waters off South Korea as a “threat” to Pyongyang and other countries of the region.

In its last previous projectile test, the North fired a barrage of missiles into the sea on August 20, despite an overture from US President Donald Trump, who said he planned to meet this year with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.

That launch from the nuclear-armed North came as South Korea and the United States held a shorter edition of their annual Ulchi Freedom Shield military exercises, following an order from Trump to scale them back.
Trump’s order alarmed US allies in the region, with the president calling the drills “inappropriate and hostile” towards North korea.
Pyongyang has long condemned US-South Korea joint exercises as rehearsals for invasion, often staging missile launches around the drills.
Trump, seeking to revive the bond he claims to have forged with Kim in his first term, told reporters at the White House on August 19 he plans to meet the North Korean leader this year.
The US president also said it was important to “get along” with Kim, adding that Pyongyang now had 57 “very powerful” nuclear weapons.
It was unusual for a US official to state a specific number on a classified issue. Seoul says the North has around 80-120 nuclear weapons.
Hours after Trump’s remarks, North Korea fired more than 10 short-range ballistic missiles from the Pyongyang area towards the Sea of Japan, South Korea’s military said.
Hours after the launches, Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of the North Korean leader, said Trump’s decision to scale back the drills with South Korea was Seoul’s punishment.

She called it in a statement “an evident disaster brought by the unrealistic and anachronistic security outlook” pursued by Seoul, arguing the South had a “master-and-servant” relationship with the United States. — AFP

c29031c026f1147a: KOTA KINABALU: People who violate Mount Kinabalu should be jailed to deter others from desecrating the sacred park in Kundasang, Ranau, deputy state secretary Datuk Jamili Nais said.
"Climbing the 4,095m mountain by encroaching on the trail network should be deemed a criminal act."

Jamili, who once served as Sabah Parks director and was a custodian of the revered mountain, said this following the recent rescue of a 46-year-old Croatian climber in a five-day operation involving dozens of personnel from various agencies.

The climber, Mauro Persic, who less than a fortnight ago took part in an extreme adventure race in the Tambatuan area of Kota Belud, ascended Mount Kinabalu via an eastern route, a trail that links to villages that depend on spring water sources in the Kundasang area.
"Climbing the sacred Mount Kinabalu without a valid permit and through an unauthorised route ought to be criminalised. Violators should spend time in jail to deter others," he said.
He said eastern Europeans had been caught committing similar violations before, using excuses such as being unaware of the regulations or not understanding the language.
"I know for a fact this is not the first time, nor will it be the last."
Trespassers would also likely defecate along the unauthorised routes they use, spoiling the natural surroundings in their wrongful quest, he said.
"Their actions defile an area considered a sacred place by the Kadazandusun, Murut and Rungus communities, including those living around the foothills of the mountain.
"When something goes wrong, they cause a lot of inconvenience and waste a lot of money in search and rescue efforts," Jamili added.
Persic sent a distress signal last weekend, triggering a rescue effort involving the Fire and Rescue Department, Sabah Parks, mountain guides, porters, medical personnel and police.

Persic appeared to have fallen and sustained injuries. Rescuers found him and, by Thursday night, brought him from about 3,000m to Timpohon Gate, the starting point of the Mount Kinabalu trail. He was then sent to the district hospital, where he is recuperating.

Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin said the whole episode serves as an important reminder to all climbers to use only official routes, engage licensed operators and strictly follow the instructions of mountain guides.

Kota Kinabalu Native Court judge Rocky Mabin said that, in addition to criminal charges that could be brought against those who violate park regulations, Native Laws could also be used to prosecute trespassers.
"Trespassers are considered disrespectful of a sacred resting place for the departed.
"This is according to the old ways of our community," Rocky said, stressing that Mount Kinabalu must be respected.
The community believes that bad things can happen if the mountain is disrespected, citing the June 5, 2015 earthquake as an example.
Seven foreign tourists had posed nude along the summit trail shortly before the earthquake. Some were eventually reprimanded and deported.
7c44d624d76250b3: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — The city’s love affair with doughnuts just got serious with Japan’s iconic I’m donut? opening its doors today.
Expect long queues outside the 2,000-square-foot store along Market Lane on the ground floor of The Exchange TRX.

Your patience will be rewarded with a chance to select your favourites from a whopping selection of more than 30 sweet and savoury nama donuts to take home in minimalist cardboard boxes featuring their logo.
This includes 16 Malaysia-exclusive flavours incorporating familiar local ingredients like Milo, Cham, pandan and coconut.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

I'm donut? Original (left) may look plain but it's all about texture with a crisp crust and light, airy interior. Inspired by 'goreng pisang', this is the Banana Fritter Caramel (right). — Pictures by Lee Khang Yi
I’m donut? comes from the brilliant mind of Japanese chef Ryouta Hirako who didn’t start out as a baker.
In his early days, he ventured into Italian food, opening his own place in Fukuoka.
When he started making bread for his restaurant, he fell into the world of flour and yeast, which led him to open the bakery Amam Dacotan and a bakery cafe Dacomecca.
Like a food fairy tale, Hirako’s nama donut was born from accidentally frying brioche dough at the bakery.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Two sandos side-by-side but with different flavour profiles: the Matcha Anko Sando (left) uses red bean paste, and the Pandan White Bean (right) combines pandan cream with white bean paste. — Picture by Choo Choy May
Their first Tokyo outlet in 2022 went viral for its unique texture coupled with creative, freshly made fillings.
The fame spread as more stores opened in Japan and they also conquered the world, expanding to New York, Seoul, Taipei and now Kuala Lumpur, which is their first South-east Asian outpost.
Hirako’s wish for the first shop in Malaysia is simple: “I just want our customers to be happy eating our donuts.”
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Don't forget the delectable filled donuts, a range of different flavours that include the Cham, inspired by the coffee-tea combined drink, and the Pandan Coconut Cream, which has toasted grated coconut inside a pandan flavoured donut and coconut cream topped with fresh coconut flesh. — Picture by Choo Choy May
For those unfamiliar with the brand or this type of donut, one question remains: Is it worth the hype?
Bite into I’m donut?’s Original—a sugar-dusted circular fried dough that puffs up like a tiny pillow—to discover a crisp crust achieved from deep-frying the dough in high heat for a short time.
This contrasts sharply with the light, fluffy interior, which uses kabocha pumpkin in the dough to reduce gluten.
For their Kuala Lumpur store, Hirako explained they swapped the pumpkin for banana, which works the same magic to create the cloud-like donuts.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Expect long queues of eager donut fans to crowd the store located at Market Lane on the ground floor of The Exchange TRX. — Picture by Choo Choy May
The texture blows your mind; it has substance yet remains soft, completely unlike other famous doughnuts that feel like you are just eating air encased in a glazed crackly sugar coating.
Even the sweetness is just right for the plain, unfilled Original with its dusting of icing sugar.
The nama donut comes in different flavours, from matcha, chocolate and a decadent Choco Shell featuring a chocolate flavoured nama donut layered with a chocolate coat and topped with cacao nibs.

Different styles include ring donuts, which are either glazed or coated with melted chocolate and nuts, like the enticing Zaku-Zaku Chocolate, which features a crunchy caramel chocolate coat and nuts covering a chocolate-flavoured donut.
There are also cream-filled donuts in different flavours like raspberry, matcha, mango and pistachio plus nama French crullers made with choux pastry and generously coated with melted chocolate.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
The open kitchen behind orange coloured glass is a hive of activity as everyone works hard to prepare the donuts, such as dipping them in chocolate. — Picture by Choo Choy May
Currently two savoury donuts are available at the counter: one with a chicken sausage and a generously stuffed Masala Chicken. In future, they hope to introduce more savoury flavours.
I’m donut? flexes its skill with its Malaysia-exclusive flavours, like the Cham-filled donuts, where tea-scented cream and coffee cream replicate the unique flavour of the two drinks.
Hirako has his favourites among the Malaysia-exclusive donuts, like Pandan White Bean and Pandan Coconut Cream.
Pandan White Bean mixes two countries — it matches smooth, sweet Japanese white bean paste (shiroan) with a silky pandan flavoured cream.
Texture makes a difference with the Pandan Coconut Cream, as pandan flavoured dough is filled with a silky coconut cream and stuffed with toasted grated coconut.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Remember to get the Zaku-Zaku Chocolate where a chocolate donut is glazed with caramel chocolate and topped with chopped nuts. — Picture by Choo Choy May
A final flourish of fresh coconut flesh strips tops each of the filled donuts.
Other local flavours mash-up include Milo-glazed, Hojicha Kaya Jam and Banana Fritter Caramel.
One local flavour you won’t see at I’m donut? is durian though as Hirako believes, “the durian is nice to eat as it is.”
Grab a matcha drink too, with 12 combinations with coffee, mocha, mango, strawberry and orange, available hot or cold. There’s also hojicha latte and juices.
Hirako also announced that they will serve premium grade Shizuoka Motoyama matcha from the Shizuoka prefecture later.
Prices for the donuts range from RM4.60 for the I’m donut? Original to RM12 for the filled donuts and sandos.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Expect long queues of eager donut fans to crowd the store located at Market Lane on the ground floor of The Exchange TRX. — Picture by Choo Choy May
The competitive pricing is close to Japan’s price range of 220 yen (RM5.80) to 480 yen (RM13).
Hirako’s rationale is to make the donuts accessible to all with this price point.
“I want the donuts to be part of Malaysian culture and to achieve that, the price must be reasonable so many customers can enjoy the donuts.”
Unlike stores in Japan that close once the donuts sell out for the day, this store will remain open because they also offer drinks, explained Dan’s Fine Food Operations Manager Shuhei Kondo.
Dan’s Fine Food holds the license for Malaysia and estimates a target of 7,000 donuts freshly made daily once operations stabilise.
Kuala Lumpur is the start for I’m donut? in Malaysia and Dan’s Fine Food confirmed that expanding their footprint is expected later, including a possible location in Johor Bahru.

c789fd4efef1f449: NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — Chinese President Xi Jinping arrives in New Delhi on Saturday for a Brics summit alongside leaders from India, Russia and Iran, as wars, trade and energy test the divided grouping.
The conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine, along with global trade turbulence and energy security, are expected to dominate the two-day meeting of the 11-nation bloc.
But Xi’s visit will also be closely watched as his first to neighbouring India since 2019, and the biggest step yet in a cautious thaw between the nuclear-armed rivals.
His arrival comes six years after a deadly 2020 military clash along their disputed Tibetan border, with ties gradually improving through restored flights, visas and high-level contacts.
Beijing said Friday it was “ready to work with India... by strengthening communication, enhancing cooperation, and properly handling differences”.
The underlying territorial dispute remains unresolved, and both sides retain heavy military deployments along their roughly 3,500-kilometre (2,175-mile) high-altitude border along Tibet.
‘Substantial harvest’
Xi is due to hold face-to-face talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi later on Saturday, according to New Delhi’s foreign ministry.
“They are looking for ‘early and substantial harvest’ when it comes to the border issue,” said Pradeep Taneja, a China-India expert at the University of Melbourne.
“You cannot have a buildup of your forces on the border... but at the same time say ‘we should continue to have people-to-people relations and economic relationships.’“
Deep mistrust remains, with their contested Himalayan frontier, a widening trade deficit and strategic rivalry still complicating ties.

Dozens of Tibetans protested in New Delhi on Friday — exiles, like their Buddhist leader the Dalai Lama, who has lived in India since fleeing a Chinese crackdown in 1959 — waving placards against Xi’s visit.
Modi on Friday embraced Russian President Vladimir Putin before talks. Putin, who last visited India in December 2025, is one of New Delhi’s most important strategic partners.
India has navigated the energy crisis caused by the US-Iran war in part by turning to Russia, despite Moscow’s war in Ukraine and pressure from Washington and other Western capitals.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, also in New Delhi on Friday, said that pressure on Iran “has reached a critical and dangerous stage” following the “military aggression by the United States and Israel”.
Modi and Pezeshkian also held talks.
India maintains cordial relations with Iran and Israel, but is also careful to strike a delicate balance in its ties with Washington.
‘Big constraint’
Brics was created in 2009 as a forum for major emerging economies seeking greater influence in institutions dominated by Western powers.
As well as Iran, Brics includes Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates — countries with sharply differing positions on the war launched by the United States and Israel in February.
UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi are also to attend.
Brazil is representated by Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira, with President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva campaigning for a fourth term in October elections.
Brics foreign ministers failed to agree on a joint statement when they met in New Delhi in May.
“The Gulf conflict is going to be the central fault line this time during the Brics summit,” said Harsh V. Pant of India’s Observer Research Foundation.
“What was seen until last year as an achievement — the expansion of Brics — today looks like a big constraint on Brics,” Pant said. — AFP
ea26cf3ef4d1c642: SANAA, Sept 12 — The Iran-backed Houthis seized control of Yemen’s entire Red Sea coast and captured three strategic islands on Friday, in a lightning offensive that cemented their hold on a vital shipping corridor linking Europe and Asia.

The developments are likely to deepen the Middle East war’s impact on international commerce, as Saudi Arabia shut down an oil pipeline following attacks, and after months of Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

Following a week-long offensive that has left hundreds dead, government officials said the Houthis seized the Yemeni side of the Bab al-Mandab Strait, the southern gateway to the Red Sea and the Suez Canal.
A local official with Yemen’s Saudi-backed government said on Friday that the Houthis had “completed their takeover of the Bab al-Mandab area and Mayyun Island”.

A government military official later reported the group had also seized Greater and Lesser Hanish, the last two islands in the narrow waterway not under their control, as well as all of the neighbouring Red Sea coastline.
“Everything that was under our control on the western coast has fallen,” the military official added.
A witness told AFP that gunmen were “deploying along the Bab al-Mandab shore and are driving around in military vehicles”.
The capture of the islands, particularly Mayyun in the middle of the strait, heightens the Houthis’ ability to attack Saudi tankers, which they have been targeting since July.
Saudi Arabia, the world’s biggest oil exporter, has relied on the Red Sea ever since Iran’s Hormuz blockade choked off its shipments via the Gulf.
Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to Iranian supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei, congratulated the Houthis on their “resounding victory” on Friday.

Oil prices have soared past US$100 (RM407) a barrel this week, while average US diesel prices topped US$6 for the first time on Friday — a potential headache for President Donald Trump ahead of midterm elections.
The Houthis’ military spokesman, Yahya Saree, said navigation through the Bab al-Mandab Strait was “safe” for all but Saudi Arabia following the latest advances.
‘Great victories’
The Houthi offensive has killed more than 500 people, according to sources on both sides.
It has also displaced about 46,000 people, the UN migration agency said on Friday.
It is part of renewed hostilities in Yemen’s civil war that began with the group’s takeover of the capital Sanaa in 2014.
Houthi supporter Abdulhamid Dhaifallah lauded the group’s “great victories” in and along the strait.
The Saudi energy ministry on Friday announced that attacks led to the closure of the pipeline — which it had been increasingly using to bypass Hormuz — adding that injuries were recorded.

“The East-West pipeline in the Riyadh and Medina regions was subjected to several attacks on Thursday morning,” a ministry official told the SPA news agency, adding: “The pipeline was stopped as a precaution, and the attacks resulted in some injuries.”

The office of Iraq’s Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi announced the dismissal of the commander in charge of the southern Maysan province following “confirmation that the attacks targeting our brethren in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia originated from a location within the governorate”.
Before the Red Sea offensive, the Houthis already controlled a large part of Yemen’s north.
They have recently attacked government-held areas in Hodeida and Taiz provinces and swept down the coast, seizing the port city of Mocha and Zuqar Island, north of Bab al-Mandab, on Thursday.
Mohamed, 46, who fled Mocha in the middle of the night, told AFP there was an “apocalyptic” atmosphere in the historic city.
Dangerous conflict
The spokesman for the Yemeni government forces, Majed Abdullah Al-Nazili, said Friday they had begun shelling areas along the Taiz-Mocha road, while residents told AFP they heard airstrikes.
While Saudi Arabia has also hit back with airstrikes and ordered troop reinforcements from Aden, where the internationally recognised government is based, it has failed to stop the Houthis’ advance.
Houthi media said two Saudi strikes hit Mocha’s airport on Friday, while a local official said the city’s seaport was hit by six missiles of unknown origin.
The ongoing exchanges risk reviving a war that killed hundreds of thousands of Yemenis and sparked one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises. — AFP
6e2b5a6ae4c56b14: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia on Thursday opened the 17th Asean Health Ministers' Meeting (AHMM) and Related Meetings, with Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad chairing the gathering for the first time in 22 years under the theme "Healthy Asean: Together Towards Equitable, Future-Ready Health Systems".

Dzulkefly, who chaired the meeting as Malaysia holds the Asean Health Ministers' chairmanship, with Myanmar as vice-chair, said the gathering marked a new phase in regional health cooperation, focusing on translating policy into action for Asean's 670 million people.

"The chain of survival is only as strong as its weakest link. Strengthening every stage is vital to securing a resilient and healthy region," he said in his opening address at the meeting here on Thursday.

The five-day conference, which began on Monday and ended yesterday, brought together health ministers and senior health officials from Asean member states, along with dialogue partners, World Health Organisation (WHO) representatives and technical experts.
BLUEPRINT FOR NEXT 5 YEARS
The centrepiece of this year's meeting was the launch of the Asean Strategic Health Agenda 2026-2030, a five-year roadmap for regional health cooperation across four core clusters.

It covers promoting healthy lifestyles and preventing non-communicable diseases, responding to all hazards and emerging public health threats, strengthening health systems and access to care and ensuring regional food safety.
Dzulkefly said the blueprint aimed to narrow health development gaps so that no Asean community or country was left behind, in line with the broader Asean Community Vision 2045.

Malaysia's chairmanship also prioritised pandemic preparedness, with the meeting expected to strengthen the operationalisation of the Asean Centre for Public Health Emergencies and Emerging Diseases, as well as developing an integrated strategy to address the dual burden of communicable and non-communicable diseases in the region.
BILATERAL MILESTONES
On the sidelines of the AHMM, Malaysia held bilateral engagements with key partners during the ministerial-level sessions.

With Singapore, both sides reaffirmed a memorandum of understanding on health cooperation, expanding collaboration in digital health, active ageing and regulatory reliance between Malaysia's Medical Device Authority and Singapore's Health Sciences Authority.
The arrangement, which took effect in March, aims to accelerate access to innovative medical devices in both countries.
With Indonesia, discussions covered digital health, traditional and complementary medicine and cross-border healthcare.
Malaysia's role as a medical tourism hub was also highlighted, with the country recording more than RM2.2 billion in medical tourism revenue last year.
Dzulkefly said he looked forward to equally strategic bilateral sessions with dialogue partners China and Japan to expand technical cooperation and investment ties in healthcare.
REGIONAL BREAKTHROUGHS
Several milestones were recorded during technical sessions preceding the ministerial-level meetings.

Malaysia chaired the inaugural Asean Roundtable Discussion on Medical Devices, where member states agreed in principle to support a phased Single Submission Model for pre-market approval, with Malaysia serving as the coordinating entry point for technical dossiers.
The model is expected to streamline medical device regulatory processes across the region and reduce time-to-market for medical innovations.
The meeting also saw the launch of the Asean Action Plan for Lung Health.

Malaysia shared its experience with artificial intelligence-assisted chest X-ray screening and proposed that Asean adopt a unified regional position to elevate lung health as a fundamental human right, in view of the growing burden of respiratory diseases.

A combined technical side event, convened under the leadership of Health Ministry director-general Datuk Dr Mahathar Abd Wahab, covered eye health through the MySPECS initiative, neglected disease research under the Drugs for Neglected Diseases initiative and behavioural insights.

Malaysia also used the occasion to advance work on rare diseases, with the handover of Malaysia's Rare Diseases Playbook taking place in support of the World Health Organisation Global Action Plan on Rare Diseases.
DIPLOMATIC DEVELOPMENTS
The AHMM also featured the inaugural Asean-United States Health Ministers' Meeting and Asean-Japan Health Ministers' Meeting.
There were also meetings with China, South Korea and WHO, which was represented by the Western Pacific Regional Office.

Dzulkefly said the platforms reflected deeper regional engagement with major global powers on issues beyond bilateral concerns, including pandemic preparedness, antimicrobial resistance and the integrity of pharmaceutical supply chains.
COMMITMENT TO ACTION
In his closing remarks, Dzulkefly said Malaysia's chairmanship would be measured not by the ambition of its agenda, but by the quality of its implementation.
"Guided by the values of Malaysia Madani, we remain firmly committed to turning health policy into tangible action for the 670 million citizens of Asean — for a better and healthier Asean."

The Health Ministry said the initiatives and policy frameworks discussed at the AHMM reflected Malaysia's commitment under the Madani framework and the consensus of Asean member states to ensure public health services remained inclusive and sustainable.

fa143723e5b3bf35: PARIS: Kylian Mbappe said he still believed he was worthy of the Ballon d'Or award despite failing to win any silverware with Real Madrid during the season, while France's World Cup campaign ended with a semi-final defeat by Spain.
In an interview with France Football, the 27-year-old hailed new France coach Zinedine Zidane and said he believed his performances merited recognition as the world's best player.

"I believe I can win it this year. It’s one of my goals, and a short-term one at that," Mbappe said. "People say I didn’t win a trophy (for club or country), but it’s an individual award. I’ve never seen a Ballon d’Or winner elected unanimously.
"Has anyone ever won with 100% of the vote? That means there’s always someone who thought the winner didn’t deserve it."

Mbappe scored 15 goals in the Champions League and 25 in La Liga before taking his World Cup tally to 22, becoming the competition's all-time leading scorer, although France's campaign ended in a 2-0 semi-final defeat by Spain.

"My idea of the Ballon d’Or comes from the Messi and Ronaldo era - you don’t give it to ordinary players, you give it to players who are different. I think I did things that were different this year, so I believe I can win it."
Asked if he thought he would be a deserving winner, Mbappe was adamant.

"There was no player better than me. We were talking about achievements. To score that many goals in the major competitions, where all the great players are, and of course at the World Cup, the biggest event, to become the competition’s all-time leading scorer - throughout my holidays, that was all people talked to me about," he said.

"It’s difficult to fully grasp what the World Cup means. It’s the competition of the great players, the stars, the greatest players in the history of the game. And to tell yourself that, at 27, I’m already the one who has scored the most goals…

"And it’s even more special because you take the record from Leo Messi, who for many people is the greatest player in history alongside Cristiano (Ronaldo). It’s fantastic. That kind of achievement is different."
The forward praised the appointment of 1998 World Cup winner Zidane, who succeeded Didier Deschamps as France's head coach.

"For French people, he means a great deal - he’s a legend, he’s the nation’s 'Zizou', he represents elegance, greatness. He made his mark on the history of the national team as a player and he had some truly iconic moments," Mbappe enthused.
"He’s perhaps the player who most embodies the France team. He’s one of those players who transcended generations. He left an indelible mark on the history of French football."

aeaf2a9d2a7e9903: PETALING JAYA: Malaysia tidak perlu mempertimbangkan kaedah pemgembirian kimia sebagai hukuman terhadap pesalah seksual, termasuk pesalah berulang, kata peguam dan pakar kriminologi.

Presiden Persatuan Peguam Wanita, Jasmine Wong, berkata hukuman itu bersandarkan andaian salah bahawa keganasan seksual didorong nafsu atau dorongan tidak terkawal, tetapi kajian menunjukkan sebaliknya.

"Kajian secara konsisten menunjukkan rogol dan keganasan seksual didorong faktor kuasa, kawalan, ketidaksamaan gender serta budaya yang menormalisasikan keganasan itu. Menganggapnya boleh dikekang secara perubatan adalah salah diagnosis terhadap masalah sebenar," katanya kepada FMT.

Wong berkata, hukuman itu bercanggah dengan hak Perlembagaan berhubung integriti badan dan kebebasan peribadi, sekali gus menimbulkan persoalan utama: adakah campur tangan perubatan tanpa persetujuan boleh dijadikan hukuman di negara ini?

Memandangkan Malaysia belum meratifikasi perjanjian antarabangsa melarang hukuman kejam, beliau berkata, terpulang kepada mahkamah untuk menentukan sama ada pengembirian kimia sesuai dilaksanakan, jika ada usaha memperkenalkannya.
Beliau turut bimbang hukuman itu mungkin dilaksanakan secara tidak konsisten memandangkan sistem keadilan jenayah Malaysia sudah menghadapi ketidaksamaan tertentu.

"Akses kepada khidmat guaman baik, kedudukan sosial dan sumber telah mempengaruhi siapa yang disabitkan berslaah serta tahap hukuman dikenakan. Hukuman begitu invasif, apabila ditambah dalam sistem mempunyai ketidaksamarataan, berisiko menjadi alat menghukum sesetengah pesalah lebih berat berbanding yang lain, bukannya menjadi pencegah sebenar."
"Dalam keadaan di mana kecenderungan konservatif dan autoritarian semakin meningkat, saya sangat berhati-hati untuk mengiktiraf campur tangan seperti ini terhadap badan seseorang."

Bekas presiden Badan Peguam, Salim Bashir, berkata tiada bukti saintifik pengembirian kimia boleh menjadi penyelesaian mutlak dalam membendung keganasan seksual, selain hukuman itu sendiri tidak berperikemanusiaan, menjatuhkan maruah dan membawa kesan berlebihan.
Salim berkata, pesalah seksual yang disabitkan kesalahan lebih wajar dikenakan pemantauan rapi dan kawal selia oleh pihak polis selepas menjalani hukuman penjara.

"Pendekatan holistik perlu dirangka untuk menguruskan rutin harian mereka, dengan aktiviti positif bagi membantu mengawal pemikiran dan tingkah laku seksual supaya mereka tidak terbabit perlakuan bersifat penderaan seksual."

Selasa lalu, Menteri Dalam Negeri Singapura, K Shanmugam dilaporkan berkata, negara itu terbuka mempertimbangkan pengembirian kimia terhadap pesalah seksual, jika terdapat bukti konklusif ia boleh mengurangkan jenayah seksual sedemikian.
Tetapi, tegasnya, bukti yang menyokong hukuman itu belum konklusif.

Negara seperti Korea, Indonesia dan Kazakhstan telah mewajibkan hukuman itu bagi kategori tertentu pesalah seksual — khususnya individu melakukan kesalahan terhadap kanak-kanak — manakala Thailand, Denmark, Jerman dan Sweden menawarkan pengembirian kimia secara sukarela.
Bukan semua kesalahan seksual didorong motivasi sama

Ahli kriminologi dari Universiti Sains Malaysia, P Sundramoorthy, berkata kesalahan seksual didorong pelbagai motivasi, termasuk dorongan seksual kompulsif, kuasa, kawalan, kemarahan, penyalahgunaan bahan atau faktor sosial lebih luas.
Katanya, ini bermakna pengembirian kimia hanya akan menangani satu komponen yang mendorong tingkah laku jenayah itu.

Jelasnya, langkah itu hanya dapat mengurangkan nafsu seks pesalah, tetapi tidak mampu menghapuskan sikap, fantasi, penyelewengan kognitif, sifat agresif, keinginan terhadap kuasa dan kawalan atau kemampuan mengeksploitasi mangsa rentan.
Walaupun terdapat bukti langkah itu boleh mengurangkan jenayah berulang sesetengah pesalah, tetapi ia tidak bermakna akan berkesan untuk semua kategori pesalah.

"Kita perlu mewujudkan rangka kerja sesuai bagi mengenal pasti pesalah berisiko tinggi, menilai punca tingkah laku jenayah mereka dan menentukan intervensi paling sesuai untuk setiap individu terlebih dahulu.

"Jika kaedah itu dipertimbangkan, ia mesti berasaskan penilaian klinikal, pengawasan kehakiman, persetujuan termaklum atau rangka kerja undang-undang jelas, pemantauan perubatan serta penilaian risiko berkala."
Undang-undang Malaysia cukup tegas, tetapi boleh diperkukuh
Wong berkata, hukuman sedia ada di Malaysia terhadap kesalahan seksual sudah cukup berat, tetapi beberapa penambahbaikan boleh dilakukan dalam aspek pemantauan dan pemulihan pesalah.
Ketika ini, jelasnya, serangan seksual terhadap kanak-kanak boleh dihukum penjara sehingga 20 tahun, manakala rogol membawa hukuman penjara maksimum 30 tahun.

"Pengawasan polis masih terhad dari segi skop dan tempoh. Kita boleh mempertimbang untuk melanjutkan pengawasan polis melebihi tiga tahun serta melaksanakan sistem pemantauan berperingkat berasaskan risiko.
"Sudah tentu, pemulihan tidak patut diserahkan kepada budi bicara kehakiman. Penilaian psikologi, terapi dan kaunseling wajib dijadikan amalan tetap, bukan bergantung kepada hakim."
Beliau turut menggesa kerajaan memperkukuh fungsi daftar pesalah seksual dengan menjadikan saringan mandatori bagi pemohon jawatan membabitkan kanak-kanak.
80ac951ea4d386f1: PETALING JAYA: There is no need for Malaysia to consider employing chemical castration as a punishment for sex offenders, even repeat offenders, say two lawyers and a criminologist.

Association of Women Lawyers president Jasmine Wong said the punishment rests on the flawed assumption that sexual violence is driven by libido or uncontrollable urges, whereas research shows otherwise.

“The research is fairly consistent that rape and sexual violence are driven by power, control, gender inequality, and a culture where such violence is normalised. Treating it as something you can medically suppress misdiagnoses the actual problem,” she told FMT.

Wong also said the punishment would clash with the constitutional right to bodily integrity and personal liberty, raising a key conundrum: can non-consensual medical intervention be imposed as a punishment here?

Since Malaysia has not ratified international treaties prohibiting cruel punishments, she said it would ultimately fall to the courts to decide whether chemical castration is appropriate, should efforts be made to introduce it.
Wong also voiced concern that the punishment could be applied inconsistently, noting that Malaysia’s criminal justice system already suffers from certain inequalities.

“Access to good legal representation, social standing and resources already shape who gets convicted, and how harshly. A punishment this invasive, layered onto a system with those existing inequalities, risks becoming another tool that hits some offenders harder than others rather than serving as a genuine deterrent.
“In a climate where conservative and authoritarian impulses are already gaining ground, I'd be very wary of legitimising this kind of state intervention over the body,” she added.

Former Bar Council president Salim Bashir said there is no scientific evidence that chemical castration could serve as a silver bullet in curbing sexual violence, adding that the punishment itself is inhumane, degrading and carries excessive consequences.
Salim said convicted sexual offenders would be better off with close monitoring and regulation by the police after serving their jail sentences.

“A holistic approach must be carved out to manage their daily routines, with positive activities to help them handle sexual thoughts and behaviours so they do not engage in sexually abusive behaviours,” he added.

On Tuesday, Singapore’s home minister K Shanmugam said the republic was open to considering chemical castrations for sex offenders if there was conclusive evidence that it could reduce such sexual crimes.
However, he said the evidence supporting the punishment remained inconclusive.

Countries like Korea, Indonesia and Kazakhstan have mandated the punishment for certain categories of sex offenders — particularly those who commit offences against minors — while Thailand, Denmark, Germany and Sweden offer chemical castration on a voluntary basis.
Not all sexual offences driven by same motivation

Criminologist P Sundramoorthy of Universiti Sains Malaysia said sexual offences are driven by various motivations. He said some perpetrators act in response to compulsive sexual urges, while others are motivated by power, control, anger, substance abuse, or broader social factors.
This means chemical castration would only address one component driving the offending behaviour, he said.

Sundramoorthy also said the measure would only reduce an offender’s sex drive, but cannot eliminate attitudes, fantasies, cognitive distortions, aggression, desire for power and control or the capacity to exploit vulnerable victims.
While there has been evidence that the measure could reduce recidivism among some convicts, this does not mean it would work across all categories of offenders, he said.
“We should first establish a proper framework for identifying high-risk offenders, assessing the causes of their offending and determining what intervention is most appropriate for each individual.

“If chemical suppression is eventually considered, it should be based on clinical assessment, judicial oversight, informed consent or a very clearly defined legal framework, regular medical monitoring and periodic risk assessment,” he said.
Malaysian law severe enough, but can be bolstered
Wong said Malaysia’s existing punishment for sex offences was severe enough, though some improvements could be made in the monitoring and rehabilitation for convicted offenders.
She said, presently, sexual assault on a child is punishable with up to 20 years in prison, while aggravated rape could see a convict punishable by the maximum 30-year jail term.
“The current police supervision is limited in scope and duration. We could consider extending police supervision beyond three years and implement a tiered risk-based monitoring system.

“And, of course, rehabilitation shouldn't be left to judicial discretion. Psychological evaluation, therapy, and counselling should be compulsory as a matter of course, not something that depends on which judge you're in front of,” she said.
Wong also urged the government to enhance the functions of its sex offender registry by making screening mandatory for individuals applying for roles that involve dealing with children.
8961c6f9afa21055: KUALA LUMPUR: Mix up a midnight margarita, and dust off your spell book, because the Owens sisters are finally back… oh my goodness, has it really been almost 30 years since audiences last saw them?
It was in 1998 when Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman first stirred up romance, witchcraft and more than a little trouble in “Practical Magic”, a whimsical film that became a beloved cult favourite.
Now they are back for another adventure. But was it truly worth the wait?
You know what they say about films that take too long to produce a sequel. And as “Practical Magic: The Book of Magic” shows, perhaps there’s some truth to that old chestnut.

The film opens with a direct callback to its predecessor. Following a tragedy, Sally Owens (Bullock) distances herself from magic, casting a spell on daughters Kylie (Joey King) and Antonia (Maisie Williams) so they forget their witchy heritage.

Magic, however, finds its way back to them. Soon, the old Owens’s family curse (which condemns any man an Owens woman falls in love with to an untimely death) rears its ugly head once again. This time, Kylie’s boyfriend Gideon (Xolo Maridueña) finds himself in danger.
Desperate to save him, Kylie turns to the very magic her mother tried to protect her from, heading to London to get to the root of her family problems.

So Sally and her sister Gillian (Kidman) set off to save her, encountering the very mysterious (and rather dashing) Professor Ian Wright (Lee Pace) on the way. But will this stranger help or hinder them?

The sequel is not without charm, although most of it is related to the first film. It’s nice to see Stockard Channing and Dianne Wiest return as elder witches Franny and Jet. Their presence immediately evokes the cosy eccentricity of the original, although their roles in this film are somewhat diminished.
There are also a few callbacks and references to events from the first film, which are integrated nicely and may even bring a tear to the eye of die-hard “Practical Magic” fans.
Story-wise, however, this Susanne Bier-directed sequel often feels long and meandering, while its stakes feel surprisingly low. Practical magic? More like practically plodding plot.

Things particularly fall apart in the third act, when the characters encounter an extremely uninspiring antagonist who feels like a second-rate henchman who wandered off the set of a Harry Potter film.

Indeed, you could say the true villain of “Practical Magic: The Book of Magic” is the dark force of Movie Cliché. You don’t need a crystal ball to see what’s coming: nearly every plot development feels tired and predictable, with twists that can be spotted several scenes away.

The acting is probably the best part of the show. It’s lovely to see Bullock and Kidman interact and banter with each other again, although these Oscar-winning actresses could probably play their roles in their sleep. Veteran actor Pace, meanwhile, brings some welcome gravitas to a role that otherwise largely amounts to male eye candy.
The new generation of Owens witches fare reasonably well, although King struggles with some of the more emotional scenes, and Williams feels underutilised.

Strangely, for a film that places so much emphasis on sisterhood, the two spend much of the runtime apart. As a result, their relationship never develops the warmth or chemistry needed to make their sisterly bond feel quite as magical as it should.

Still, it’s always refreshing to see a film with such a female-dominated cast, all of whom seem to be having a wickedly good time. And if you’re simply looking for a celebration of sisterhood, there’s enough warmth and witchiness here for a decent girls’ night out.
For everyone else, however, “Practical Magic: The Book of Magic” is unlikely to cast much of a spell. After such a long wait, maybe fans deserved something a little more magical.
As of press time, ‘Practical Magic: The Book of Magic’ is screening in cinemas nationwide.
775098e559f7c45f: BOSTON, (United States): A federal judge on Friday blocked US President Donald Trump's administration from continuing to ask applicants for civil service jobs throughout the government to respond to what unions described as a partisan "loyalty question."

US District Judge George O'Toole in Boston sided with three unions representing government workers who sued last year after the administration began asking applicants for nonpartisan federal jobs to write essays explaining how they would help advance Trump's policies and executive orders.

The unions, including the American Federation of Government Employees, argued the question mandated by the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) unlawfully politicized the hiring process for career government workers by attempting to assess their support for the Republican president.

O'Toole, an appointee of Democratic President Bill Clinton, said the question had been asked of applicants to positions ranging from an air traffic control specialist to a crane operator to a nuclear materials courier.

He said the unions' members reasonably interpreted it as an attempt to determine the applicants' political views, even though the Civil Service Reform Act bars making employment decisions for such jobs on the basis of political affiliation.

"The plaintiffs are thus likely to succeed in showing that there is no legitimate governmental interest in inquiring into the political beliefs of applicants to federal civil service vacancies," O'Toole wrote.
The judge halted the use of the question on grounds that it likely violated the Administrative Procedure Act by infringing on speech rights under the US Constitution's First Amendment.

Lawyers for the unions at the liberal group Democracy Forward welcomed the ruling, saying that over 70,000 federal job postings had included the question, undermining what is supposed to be a merit-based hiring system.
"Requiring federal job applicants to answer politically motivated questions goes against the very nature of the nonpartisan civil service," AFGE National President Everett Kelley said in a statement.
The other two unions are the American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees and the National Association of Government Employees.

OPM did not immediately respond to a request for comment. It has previously defended the question as optional and said that it had been clear that hiring decisions could not be based on political beliefs.

It had adopted the question in response to an executive order Trump signed in January 2025 that required it to develop a hiring plan that brought into the federal workforce "only highly skilled Americans dedicated to the furtherance of American ideals, values, and interests."

OPM in a May 2025 memo to the heads of all executive agencies set forth various actions to implement Trump's order, including by requiring that job applicants be asked to respond to the essay question.
b134061dc950329d: MADRID: Formula One championship leader Kimi Antonelli lapped fastest for Mercedes in free practice at Madrid's new Spanish Grand Prix circuit on Friday with Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton close behind.

Second in a first practice led by teammate George Russell, Antonelli then set the pace in a later session halted briefly by Racing Bulls' British rookie Arvid Lindblad becoming the first F1 driver to crash at the Madring and bring out red flags.
"It is a very cool circuit to drive around. It is a real challenge for us as drivers, with lots of high-speed corners and walls close by," said Antonelli.

fdfc0aa6747d969f: SAN FRANCISCO: Anthropic is in talks to bring Nvidia as an anchor investor into what could be the largest initial public offering in history, two people familiar with the matter told Reuters.

Anthropic is seeking to raise as much as US$100 billion that could value the artificial intelligence startup at around US$2 trillion, the people said. Nvidia is considering investing up to $10 billion in the IPO, one of the sources added. The plans remain under discussion and could change, they cautioned, requesting anonymity because the discussions are confidential.

Nvidia’s potential involvement in the IPO, which has not previously been reported, would give Anthropic an early strategic backer for the outsized offering, while further deepening ties between the chipmaker and one of its major customers.

Bringing a deep-pocketed anchor investor like Nvidia onboard could boost investor confidence in the listing, which is shaping up to be a major test of public-market appetite for the enormous valuations and capital requirements of frontier AI labs.
Anthropic declined to comment. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Anchor investors are typically institutional investors that commit to buy a set portion of an IPO before it is marketed more broadly, providing an early vote of confidence in the shares. It is increasingly common for mega IPOs to line up early institutional commitments, given the large amounts they seek to raise.
Chip designer Arm’s anchor investors included Nvidia and Amazon, while Saudi Arabia’s PIF was among SpaceX’s anchor investors.

The deepened relationship highlights the complex ties between AI model developers and the companies supplying the enormous amounts of computing power they require. Anthropic relies heavily on Nvidia GPUs, while also seeking to diversify its chip suppliers as demand for Claude has strained its available computing capacity.

In November 2025, Nvidia said it would invest up to US$10 billion in the AI startup as part of a broader partnership under which Anthropic committed to buy US$30 billion of Microsoft Azure computing capacity powered by Nvidia chips.

Anthropic already counts the biggest tech companies in the world as backers. These include Amazon and Google, who are also its major compute suppliers. In April, Anthropic said it would commit more than US$100 billion over a decade to Amazon’s AWS, while using more than 1 million of Amazon’s Trainium2 chips. It has also agreed with Google and Broadcom to add multiple gigawatts of TPU capacity.

The company has been trying to access more compute as its revenue has surged. It is also working to gain greater control over its hardware costs by forming an in-house team to design custom chips tailored to Claude.

The listing, which is expected to complete before the US midterm elections in November, would mark another jump in Anthropic’s valuation. The Claude maker raised US$65 billion in May at a post-money valuation of US$965 billion. Its annualised revenue run rate had climbed above US$65 billion by the end of July, from about US$9 billion at the end of 2025, according to the company.
The potential valuation also hinges in part on company projections of roughly US$190 billion to US$200 billion in revenue in 2028, Reuters previously reported.
The expected Anthropic IPO added to a string of blockbuster listings that has propelled the US IPO market toward a record year, following Elon Musk's SpaceX's debut in June.
US IPOs, excluding special-purpose acquisition companies, have raised a record US$137 billion through the end of August, according to Dealogic.

aafe631c64d53194: PETALING JAYA: There was nothing particularly sophisticated about the video that helped turn Tucker Budzyn into an internet star.
He was a fluffy golden retriever puppy, barely a few months old, confronted with an ice cube. Tucker pawed at it, puzzled over it, and behaved exactly as a curious puppy might.

His human Courtney Budzyn created an Instagram account in 2018 shortly after bringing him back to her home in Michigan, United States, at eight weeks old. The profile was largely to share his antics with friends and family.

The ice-cube clip went viral the following month. By six months old, Tucker already had some 60,000 followers - marking the beginning of something neither Courtney nor her husband Mike could have imagined.
Over the next eight years, Tucker became one of the world’s best-known dogs, attracting millions of followers across TikTok, YouTube, Instagram and Facebook.
His success eventually grew large enough for Courtney and Mike to leave their respective jobs and devote themselves to Tucker and his online world full-time.

But numbers only partly explain why people loved him. Tucker had the sort of face onto which humans could project an entire conversation: soulful eyes, extravagant expressions and an apparent opinion about almost everything.

His videos turned the ordinary business of being a dog into comedy. There were food tastings, swimming sessions, family adventures and playful “conversations” supplied by Courtney, who gave voice to what Tucker might supposedly have been thinking.
Fans have described Tucker’s videos as a source of comfort during lonely or difficult periods, while his expressive personality made people who had never met him feel oddly familiar with him.

Later, Tucker shared the spotlight with Todd, another golden retriever affectionately presented to fans as his “son”. Their wrestling, mischief and domestic adventures became part of an online world followers returned to again and again.
A diagnosis, then hope
On Aug 30, Tucker's fans and followers were shaken when Courtney revealed that, at age eight, he had been diagnosed with lymphoma about two weeks earlier.

There was reason for optimism. He had begun chemotherapy and, after initially responding well, was considered to be in partial remission. Despite some side effects, Tucker was still walking, swimming and enjoying the things that made him happy.
Courtney said her priority was his quality of life. And in what would become an unexpectedly precious gift, Tucker’s final weeks were filled with remarkably ordinary pleasures.
He went to the park several times and made a point of marking just about every tree he could find. He went swimming. His first leap into the pool on both occasions was still strong and enthusiastic.

He wrestled with Todd in the backyard, rolled in the grass and felt the breeze through his fur. He even went rollerblading with Courtney. And twice a day, there was chicken - to accompany his medication, although Tucker presumably had few objections to that arrangement.

Then everything changed with frightening speed. According to Courtney, as treatment successfully attacked the cancer in his intestine, a hole had been left in the affected area, resulting in an infection that seemed to strike overnight.
The family rushed him for emergency veterinary care. He was weak and was given antibiotics and fluids, but his fever continued to rise. They could not bring it down.
On Sept 2, his family had to make the decision every pet owner dreads: to let him go. He was only eight.
Three days later, Courtney appeared before the audience that had followed Tucker almost his entire life. She told followers that Tucker was gone.

In the tearful tribute, she spoke of having tried everything she could to save him. She also struggled to describe the scale of the loss, saying Tucker had become “part of my soul” and that losing him felt like losing part of herself.
Yet amidst the grief, she returned to those final weeks - the parks, swimming, grass, chicken, and time with Todd. There was consolation in knowing that Tucker had still been Tucker.

Fans responded to his death by filling his social media pages with condolences and memories, many describing Tucker as one of the first pet influencers they had followed, and recalling how reliably his videos had made them smile.
His story will also continue in another form. A children’s picture book, “Of All the Sniffs I Love the Most”, is scheduled for release on Nov 17.
Written around Tucker’s adventures and his bond with his family, its message is ultimately a simple one: adventures may come and go, but being close to those you love matters most.

Tucker spent eight years teaching millions of strangers that joy could be found in the simple pleasures in life. And perhaps that is why saying goodbye to an internet-famous dog feels so personal to so many.
Somewhere along the way, he stopped feeling like somebody else’s golden retriever and became, in some small way, everybody’s dog.

fd73ca2fee6a8203: At 2pm on Sept 4, the air pollutant index (API) in Serian, Sarawak, hit 521. Anything above 300 is "hazardous", and the Yang di-Pertuan Agong consented that same day to an emergency across the Serian division, the first haze emergency this country has declared since Port Klang in 2005, and Sarawak's first since 1997.
Sarawak shut 647 schools across 12 districts for the week, sending almost 200,000 children home. The emergency was lifted on Sept 7. The following morning, Serian’s API was back at 302.

Indonesia's ministry of forestry says land was illegally sold and then burned for oil palm. Indonesian police have arrested 72 people over 89 arson cases, and the Indonesian environmental group Walhi found that 74% of Kalimantan's hotspots sat inside corporate concessions.
El Niño dried the peat, somebody struck the match.
Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Aug 8 that "if there are Malaysian companies involved, we give room for Indonesia to take action. We certainly will not defend them."
He is right, but "we will not defend them" is a promise not to obstruct, not a promise to act.
What the smoke is costing us
The health ministry's sentinel clinics logged 61 asthma cases in the second week of August. By the last week of the month, the figure was 1,811.

The World Bank put the bill for Indonesia's 2015 fires at US$16.1 billion (RM65 billion), and a study in Scientific Reports estimated that that season caused between 6,150 and 17,270 premature deaths across Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore in two months.
So can this be solved for good? Not by one law, and not by one country.

The haze is a chain: fire is the cheapest way to clear land, drained peat lets that fire smoulder for months, the penalties in the country where it burns are rarely collected, and the buyers abroad rarely ask.
Break enough of those links and the odds shift in our favour. Four things would do that, and only one of them is Malaysia's alone.
1. Make the match the expensive option

Indonesia already has the law but implementation seems to be the problem. Environmental groups say more than US$220 million in environmental fines from plantation and timber companies found liable for fires remain uncollected.
Indonesian courts also tend to demand proof that any named executive intended the harm, which is why arrests on the ground so rarely reach a boardroom.

Enforcement in Jakarta cannot be Malaysia's job, but Malaysia can close its own gaps. It can pass the Transboundary Haze Act that the Pakatan Harapan Cabinet agreed to in principle on Feb 12, 2020, modelled on Singapore's 2014 law with fines of up to S$100,000 (RM319,000) a day and a presumption that fire on your concession is your responsibility.
Also have Bursa Malaysia require listed planters to publish their Indonesian concession maps.

Then make burning unnecessary. Asean's new Investment Framework for Haze-Free Sustainable Land Management could fund mechanical clearing for the smallholders who reach for a match because a machine costs more.
Also, one has to keep in mind that the European Union's deforestation rules, to be in force from Dec 30, 2026, will demand geolocated proof that palm oil did not come from cleared land.
2. Rewet the peat
Peat burns for months because plantation canals have drained it; the peat watchdog Pantau Gambut warns it will stay flammable year-round as long as those canals are left open.
A 2026 study of 3,840 canal blocks in Kalimantan found the best-placed ones cut fire occurrence by up to 15.6%, with carbon offsets covering up to 30% of the cost of building them.
That is not a cure, but it is measurable, and West Kalimantan is the province whose smoke lands in Kuching.
3. Give Asean's haze machinery teeth
The Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution has existed since 2002 and every member has ratified it, yet it cannot compel anyone to prosecute anyone.
The body meant to give it operational muscle, a Coordinating Centre in Jakarta, was created by a separate agreement that members were still ratifying as of July, so the centre is not yet in force.
Meanwhile, the second haze-free roadmap promises a haze-free Asean by 2030, four years away.

This is where Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brunei have to move together, because smoke from Kalimantan lands in Kuching, smoke from Sumatra lands in Singapore and Selangor, and Thailand has its own northern burning season.

Malaysia proposed a bigger Asean haze fund and "science diplomacy" in Bali in July; the parties meet again in Da Nang in October. Ratify the centre, fund it, and get it to publish daily hotspot-to-concession matches across every member's satellite, the "reciprocal disclosure" Greenpeace Malaysia asked for last week.
4. Protect the children while the rest takes hold

Cloud seeding is a comfort, not a cure, and Deputy Prime Minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi conceded as much when he said Malaysia's operation continued "depending on the wind direction and location of the clouds".

What actually protects a child is filtered indoor air. Rather than closing 647 schools, Sarawak could fit them with HEPA filtration; and stockpile N95 masks in every klinik kesihatan before the next El Niño.
None of this guarantees a clear sky in 2027, but breaking four links in the chain of causes is better than breaking none.
If the region does its part alongside Indonesia, the haze has a real chance of becoming what Asean's own haze-free roadmap already promises on paper: a memory.

21131c77b8a20173: PETALING JAYA: Rang Undang-Undang (RUU) e-dagang perlu menekankan tanggungjawab penyedia platform jualan dalam mencegah kegiatan penjualan dadah secara dalam talian, kata Gabungan Persatuan Pengguna Malaysia (Fomca).

Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif Fomca T Saravanan berkata platform tidak boleh mengatakan mereka hanya menyediakan ruang kepada penjual dan tidak bertanggungjawab terhadap sebarang transaksi termasuk produk dijual.
Menurutnya, pihak terbabit menyediakan akses kepada pengguna, sistem pemasaran, algoritma, komunikasi dan dalam banyak keadaan kemudahan transaksi.

"Kalau platform mempunyai teknologi mengetahui barang dicari, mencadangkan produk dan menyasarkan iklan kepada pengguna, teknologi sama sepatutnya digunakan untuk mengesan serta menyekat produk terlarang dan berbahaya.
"Mereka juga mempunyai tanggungjawab memastikan platform mereka tidak digunakan untuk menjual produk yang menyalahi undang-undang atau membahayakan pengguna," katanya kepada FMT.
"Sebab itu Fomca berpandangan kerajaan perlu mempercepatkan penggubalan Akta E-Dagang yang komprehensif, dengan tanggungjawab platform dinyatakan secara jelas."

Baru-baru ini, Menteri Komunikasi Fahmi Fadzil mendedahkan kebimbangan Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim terhadap kegiatan penjualan dadah secara dalam talian, termasuk fentanil dan bahan disebut sebagai 'piu-piu' yang merisaukan.
Sehubungan itu, Suruhanjaya Komunikasi dan Multimedia Malaysia (SKMM) diarahkan mengadakan pertemuan dengan platform e-dagang untuk mengatasi isu berkenaan.
Saravanan turut menggesa akta itu turut mewajibkan produk dijual secara dalam talian mematuhi keperluan dari aspek pelesenan, pensijilan, pematuhan standard, pelabelan dan maklumat keselamatan.

"Sekiranya platform berulang kali membenarkan penjualan produk terlarang atau berbahaya walaupun telah diberikan amaran, tindakan penguatkuasaan tegas perlu diambil termasuk penalti setimpal," katanya.

Presiden Persatuan Pengguna Siber Malaysia Siraj Jalil pula berkata platform yang tidak lagi wajar berlindung di sebalik status perantara pasif, ketika mereka mengaut keuntungan daripada yuran transaksi atau iklan.

"Dari sudut kebertanggungjawaban, kegagalan berulang selepas amaran pihak berkuasa wajar diklasifikasikan sebagai kecuaian operasi boleh dikenakan liabiliti vikarius dan penalti kewangan mandatori berasaskan peratusan perolehan tahunan.
"Selain itu penggantungan lesen operasi, mahupun tuntutan ganti rugi sivil oleh pihak terjejas," katanya.
Beliau berkata sekatan kata kunci semata-mata juga terbukti lapuk dan tidak memadai kerana sindiket dengan mudah boleh memintas sistem.
"Menggunakan istilah slanga, leetspeak, kod emoji, atau menyembunyikan maklumat jualan di dalam poster grafik.

"Bagi menutup ruang ini, platform perlu mewajibkan penggunaan kecerdasan buatan (AI) multimodal yang berupaya menganalisis teks, imej pembungkusan produk, dan teknologi OCR serentak sebelum sesuatu iklan dibenarkan terbit," katanya.

Menurutnya, langkah teknologi itu mesti diperkukuh dengan prosedur pengesahan identiti penjual (e-KYC) bertaraf perbankan melibatkan padanan biometrik MyKad atau pasport, pendaftaran perniagaan Suruhanjaya Syarikat Malaysi (SSM) serta akaun bank yang sah.

"Penguatkuasaan jejak peranti (device fingerprinting) juga kritikal bagi membolehkan sekatan perkakasan (hardware ban) dilaksanakan, sekali gus menghalang penjual sama membuka akaun baharu melalui peranti atau rangkaian," katanya.
